chat.author: Thomas Fossati
chat.text: Mike: Sealing involves binding a secret, e.g., as a decryption key, to a set of expected integrity register values (in TPM parlance, PCRs).  The PCRs are computed from the entries in a log.  For the computation to be deterministic, the logged events need to be stable (hence using the "extracted", form).

The authors of pkix-attest have been talking about a very similar problem over the past few weeks, and that's that when Evidence needs to be parsed within a constrained, maybe offline, environment that can't afford a super lenient parser, then protocol extension points become a liability because as soon as some producer exercises those extension points, you fail to have interop.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
zhang jun said:

i mean one kind of the implementation is to let the lead verifier decides the nonce, while this nonce can be generated by itself, or based on the entropy from itself and other component verifiers.

if the lead<->lead nonce is derived from a TLS exporter, or equivalent, then it is never actually transmitted, so when compromised lead verifier changes what it provides to components,  (and lead verifier splits things up for component verifiers), then the attempt to re-use the component evidence would, yes, be defeated.
